items.title: 1.8.1 Method of Constructing the Graph of an Inverse Function (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Pichle topic mein hum ne parha ke function aur us ke inverse ke graph line \(y = x\) mein ek doosre ka aaina hote hain. Ab is baat ko amli tareeqe mein badalte hain: kisi one-to-one function ka graph diya ho to us ke inverse ka graph kaise banayein? Socho jaise aap kaaghaz ko line \(y = x\) par tah (fold) kar dein; ek taraf ki tasveer doosri taraf chhap jaye. Wahi chhapi hui tasveer inverse ka graph hai.
Kitab ke mutabiq inverse function ka graph geometry se is tarah banta hai:

items: (i) Draw the graph of the given one-to-one function.
(ii) Consider the line \(y = x\) on the same coordinate plane.
(iii) Reflect the graph of the function about the line \(y = x\).
(iv) The resulting reflected curve represents the graph of the inverse function.

blocks.text: Kitab ki wazahat: reflection is baat ki zamanat deta hai ke asal graph ka har point inverse graph ke ek mutabiq (corresponding) point par jata hai, aur dono line \(y = x\) se barabar perpendicular faasle par rehte hain. Is tarah dono graphs ki geometric symmetry qaim rehti hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Amli taur par \(y = x\) mein reflection bohat aasan hai: coordinates ki jagah badal dein. Point \((p, q)\) ban jata hai \((q, p)\). Misaal: \((2, 5)\) ka aaina \((5, 2)\).
Yeh sach mein aaina kyun hai? \((p, q)\) aur \((q, p)\) ka midpoint \(\left(\frac{p+q}{2}, \frac{p+q}{2}\right)\) hai, jis ke dono coordinates barabar hain, yani yeh \(y = x\) par hai. Aur in do points ko jorne wali line ka slope \(-1\) hai, jo \(y = x\) (slope 1) par perpendicular hai. Is liye dono points line se barabar faasle par hain, bilkul jaise kitab kehti hai.
Khaas nishaniyan bhi apni jagah badalti hain: ek axis ka intercept doosri axis ka intercept ban jata hai, aur horizontal asymptote vertical asymptote ban jata hai.
Khud sochiye: point \((0, 1)\) ka \(y = x\) mein aaina kya hai? (Jawab: \((1, 0)\).)
Ab kitab ki misaal mein yahi tareeqa lagate hain. Yeh misaal is liye ahem hai ke yeh topic 1.6 ki baat ko graph se saabit karti hai: natural log, exponential ka inverse hai.

blocks.title: Example 12
blocks.problem: (Logarithmic Graph from Exponential Graph) Show graphically that the function \(y = \ln x\) is the inverse of the function \(y = e^{x}\).
steps:
Diya gaya: exponential function \(y = e^{x}\).
Maloom karna (saabit karna): graph ke zariye ke \(y = \ln x\) is ka inverse hai.
Tareeqa: 1.8.1 wala tareeqa. Pehle tasalli karenge ke \(y = e^{x}\) one-to-one hai (warna inverse banta hi nahi), phir us ke graph ko line \(y = x\) mein reflect karenge, aur dekhenge ke jo curve bana woh kaun sa hai.

Step 1: Function invertible hai
Exponential function \(y = e^{x}\) lijiye. Yeh \(]-\infty, \infty[\) par one to one hai aur is ka range \(]0, \infty[\) hai. Is liye yeh invertible hai aur is ka inverse \(]0, \infty[\) par defined hoga.
Kyun: topic 1.8 ke mutabiq one-to-one function (co-domain = range ke saath) ka inverse hota hai. Aur \(e^{x}\) ka range, inverse ka domain ban jata hai; isi liye inverse sirf positive \(x\) par chalega.

Step 2: \(y = e^{x}\) aur line \(y = x\) banayein
Ab \(y = e^{x}\) ka graph aur line \(y = x\) ek hi axes par banate hain (Figure 1.13). \(y = e^{x}\) ke kuch points (values round ki hui):
\[x = -2,\ -1,\ 0,\ 1,\ 2\]
\[e^{x} \approx 0.14,\ 0.37,\ 1,\ 2.72,\ 7.39\]
Kyun: tareeqe ke step (i) aur (ii): pehle asal function ka graph, phir usi plane par aaina wali line.
Dhyan dein: \(e^{x}\) kabhi zero ya negative nahi hota; \(x = -2\) par bhi value positive (0.14) hai.

Step 3: Points ko y = x mein reflect karein
Inverse ka graph pane ke liye \(y = e^{x}\) ke points ko line \(y = x\) mein reflect karte hain. \(y = x\) mein reflection ka matlab seedha hai: coordinates ki jagah badal do:
\[(-2,\ 0.14) \to (0.14,\ -2)\]
\[(-1,\ 0.37) \to (0.37,\ -1)\]
\[(0,\ 1) \to (1,\ 0)\]
\[(1,\ 2.72) \to (2.72,\ 1)\]
\[(2,\ 7.39) \to (7.39,\ 2)\]
Kyun: tareeqe ka step (iii). Point \((p, q)\) aur us ke aaine \((q, p)\) ka midpoint \(y = x\) par hota hai, aur un ko jorne wali line \(y = x\) par perpendicular hoti hai. Is liye dono line se barabar faasle par hain. Figure 1.13 ki dashed lines yahi dikhati hain.

Step 4: Reflect hue points ko jorein
Ab in reflect hue points se guzarne wala curve banate hain (Figure 1.13). Yeh curve is function ko dikhata hai:
\[y = \ln x\]
jo saaf taur par interval \(]0, \infty[\) par defined hai.
Kyun: tareeqe ka step (iv). Har reflect hua point \((e^{p}, p)\) equation \(y = \ln x\) ko poora karta hai, kyun ke \(\ln(e^{p}) = p\) (log aur exponential ek doosre ko cancel karte hain).

Tasdeeq:
Table se: \(\ln 1 = 0\), \(\ln 2.72 \approx 1\), \(\ln 0.37 \approx -1\), \(\ln 7.39 \approx 2\). Algebra se bhi: \(y = e^{x}\) mein \(x\) aur \(y\) badlein to \(x = e^{y}\), yani \(y = \ln x\). Nishaniyan bhi badal gayin: \(e^{x}\) ka horizontal asymptote \(y = 0\) aur point \((0, 1)\); \(\ln x\) ka vertical asymptote \(x = 0\) aur point \((1, 0)\). Sab kuch match karta hai.
blocks.answer: \(y = e^{x}\) ke graph ka line \(y = x\) mein reflection \(y = \ln x\) ka graph hai. Is liye \(y = \ln x\), \(y = e^{x}\) ka inverse hai.

blocks.alt: Grid graph on a pale yellow panel, x and y from minus 5 to 5. The blue curve y = e to the power x, the green curve y = ln x and the red line y = x, with arrows. Dots on the blue curve are joined by dashed lines, at right angles to y = x, to their mirror-image dots on the green curve; for example (0, 1) is joined to (1, 0).
blocks.caption: Figure 1.13: y = ln x as the reflection of y = e^x in the line y = x (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Figure 1.13 ko ghor se dekhiye. Neela curve \(y = e^{x}\) hai, sabz curve \(y = \ln x\), aur laal line \(y = x\). Har dashed line ek neele point ko us ke sabz jode se milati hai, aur har dashed line laal line ko theek beech mein, seedhe zaviye (right angle) par kaat-ti hai. Baayen taraf \(e^{x}\) ke points \(x\)-axis ke bohat qareeb hain (jaise \((-5, 0.0067)\)); un ke aaine \(y\)-axis ke bohat qareeb neeche chale gaye hain (jaise \((0.0067, -5)\)). Yahi wajah hai ke \(e^{x}\) ka horizontal asymptote, \(\ln x\) ka vertical asymptote ban gaya.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh misaal hamari taraf se hai (kitab ka sawal nahi): \(y = 2^{x}\) ke graph se \(y = \log_2 x\) ka graph banaiye.
Step 1: \(2^{x}\) one-to-one hai, range \(]0, \infty[\); is liye inverse \(]0, \infty[\) par hoga.
Step 2: \(2^{x}\) ke points: \((-2, \frac{1}{4})\), \((-1, \frac{1}{2})\), \((0, 1)\), \((1, 2)\), \((2, 4)\), \((3, 8)\).
Step 3: coordinates badlein: \((\frac{1}{4}, -2)\), \((\frac{1}{2}, -1)\), \((1, 0)\), \((2, 1)\), \((4, 2)\), \((8, 3)\).
Step 4: in ko jorein; yeh \(y = \log_2 x\) hai. Tasdeeq: \(\log_2 8 = 3\), kyun ke \(2^{3} = 8\). Yeh wahi points hain jo topic 1.6.2 mein \(\log_2 x\) ke liye liye the.
Khud sochiye: \(y = (\frac{1}{2})^{x}\) ko \(y = x\) mein reflect karein to kaun sa function milega? (Jawab: \(y = \log_{1/2} x\).)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(f^{-1}\) ka graph: \(f\) banao, \(y = x\) banao, reflect karo; jo tasveer bane woh \(f^{-1}\) hai.
2. \(y = x\) mein reflection: \((p, q) \to (q, p)\).
3. \(y = \ln x\), \(y = e^{x}\) ka aaina hai: \((0, 1) \to (1, 0)\), asymptote \(y = 0 \to x = 0\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Aise function ko reflect karna jo one-to-one nahi (jaise \(\mathbb{R}\) par \(|x|\) ya \(x^{2}\)): phir aaine wali tasveer function ka graph hi nahi rehti, kyun ke ek \(x\) par do \(y\) aa jate hain.
2. \(\ln x\) ko \(x \le 0\) par banana ya \(y\)-axis ke paar le jana. \(\ln x\) sirf \(x > 0\) par hai.
3. Points ko seedha upar-neeche ya daayen-baayen khiskana. Reflection hamesha \(y = x\) par perpendicular hota hai, yani coordinates ki adla badli.
